biggest_catch: Applying never guarantees a response — employers choose who to interview.
catches: No payment handled by the platform — offers and pay are negotiated with each employer.
Some roles carry location or schedule requirements despite flexible labels.
Applying does not guarantee any employer response.
The platform centers moms and women; roles target work-life integration needs.

c1.evidence: The Mom Project's official talent page (work.themomproject.com/talent-community) states: 'Create your job profile and set your preferences on roles you're interested in. Find and apply to jobs from family-friendly employers. Get notified when jobs match your preferences. Receive invites from employers to apply and interview for roles.' — a live, provider-owned deal channel with hundreds of active listings observed this session.

c2.evidence: Official pages publish no fixed pay range — compensation is set per employer; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official community guide: complete the Talent Profile, check job alerts, apply to opportunities, track status in the Talent Dashboard.

c4.evidence: No fee appears on official talent pages for creating a profile or applying; joining is described as free.

eligibility: Anyone able to meet listed role requirements; the platform centers moms seeking flexible, family-friendly work.
notes: Scenario: niche job board. The Mom Project connects talent with family-friendly employers offering flexible, remote, and contract roles — with job alerts, employer invites, mentorship (Rally), and resources. Pay is per employer and negotiated — variable, never guaranteed.

steps: Create your Talent Profile on The Mom Project with experience, skills, and work preferences.
Check job alerts for new matching roles or proactively search opportunities.
Apply to opportunities that fit your experience and preferences.
Track application status in your Talent Dashboard and interview with employers who engage.
